empty.no_agents: no agents yet. start claude, codex or pi in a terminal
prompt.name: Name
setup.busy_update: Updating herdr-core… your terminals keep running.
setup.connect_foot: Once you've resolved this, try again.
setup.install_foot: Install it for me puts it in {place} (with hc), like its own installer: {install}
setup.missing_body: Your herdr-core can't do everything this Herdr needs ({methods}). Updating keeps your terminals running.
setup.needs_body: herdr-core runs your terminals and agents, and keeps them alive when this window closes. Herdr couldn't find it on this computer.
setup.newer_body: Your herdr-core speaks a newer protocol (generation {generation}) than this Herdr understands. Update Herdr; your terminals keep running.
setup.newer_title: This Herdr is older than your herdr-core
setup.or_hc_update: Or update it yourself: hc update
setup.too_old_body: Yours is {have}; this Herdr needs {need} or newer. Updating keeps your terminals running.
toast.edits_body: Herdr's own layouts and mods can't be changed: clone one to make it yours.
toast.missing_mods_body: Showing Herdr instead. Missing: {missing}. Your {name} layout file is still there.
machine_add.body: A VPS, a Mac mini, a box at home: Herdr reaches it over ssh, and agents there keep running while your laptop sleeps.
machine_add.mac_body: macOS asks on the Mac's own screen before an agent reads Desktop, Documents or Downloads, and waits until someone answers. Give herdr-core Full Disk Access there and it never asks again: in the list, press + and pick this file:
machine_add.mac_opened: It's open on the Mac's screen.
machine_add.mac_title: {name} is a Mac: allow its folders once
machine_add.needs_you: Couldn't add {target} here: it needs you to answer something (a password, a new host key, or installing herdr-core there). Run `{command}` in a terminal. `hc machine --help` shows the options.
machine_add.no_hosts: Your ssh config lists no hosts
machine_add.or_type: Or type how ssh reaches it
machine_add.title: Add a machine
picker.placeholder: Go to a tab, space or agent…
picker.title: Go to…
worktree.changed: It changed since this opened. Enter again removes it anyway.
worktree.dirty: It has uncommitted changes: they will be lost.
worktree.is_main: This is the repository's main checkout, not a worktree.
worktree.new_detail: A new space on a checkout in {path}. A branch that exists is checked out; a new one starts from here.
worktree.not_repo: {path} is not in a git repository.
worktree.not_repo_folder: This folder is not in a git repository.
worktree.remote_home: Could not find the remote home folder.
worktree.remove_detail: Closes the space and deletes {path}. The branch stays.
worktree.unpushed: Submodule {names} has commits that aren't pushed anywhere: they will be lost.
feedback.agent_draft: Drafted by an agent: read it before sending
feedback.email_label: Email: only if you want a reply
feedback.message_label: Your message (up to 4000 characters). Paste or drop screenshots, up to 3.
feedback.placeholder: What happened? What did you expect?
feedback.preview_label: What we send: exactly this JSON, plus the screenshots above. No logs or install ID.
feedback.sent: Sent. Thanks for helping us improve Herdr.
feedback.source_build: This build was made from source and doesn't send feedback. Use a release build.
feedback.title: Send feedback
whatsnew.title: What's new in Herdr
welcome.add_later: Not now? Add machine is at the bottom of the sidebar too.
welcome.agents_helpers_body: They show up under the agent that started them. Click one to watch it.
welcome.agents_need_body: A ring while one works, “{needs}” when it asks something, a sound when it finishes.
welcome.agents_need_title: Agents tell you when they need you
welcome.ask_prompt: Read ~/.config/herdr-app/AGENTS.md, then tell me what you can change in Herdr.
welcome.feedback_hint: Something off or missing? {settings} › {send}. We read every one.
welcome.from_herdr_migrate: Want your keybinds and settings carried over? Give your agent this line:
welcome.from_herdr_new: This is a new app on a new core. Your herdr workspaces stay where they are; nothing moves over.
welcome.from_herdr_same: Same idea as before: spaces, tabs and terminals.
welcome.machines_body: A server or a Mac mini runs its own herdr-core, so its agents keep going even while this laptop sleeps.
welcome.machines_title: Your other machines, in the same window
welcome.migrate_prompt: Read `herdr-app --skill`, then migrate my keybinds and settings from ~/.config/herdr/config.toml
welcome.more_examples_body: {settings} › Look has more layouts to try or start from, Herdr 98 among them. Your agent can copy any of them and change anything.
welcome.one_key_body: It opens the command palette, with every action by name and its key. It works the same in every layout.
welcome.outside_body: hc is herdr-core's command line. In any terminal, hc ls lists everything running and hc attach t3 jumps into one. Your agents can use it to start and watch other agents for you. Tell them to read hc's help, or make it a skill.
welcome.outside_title: Your terminals, outside this window too
welcome.page1_body: The terminals and agents you open here don't live in this window. They run in herdr-core, a small background program on your computer. Close Herdr, update it, or let it crash, and your agents keep working. Open it again and everything is where you left it, as long as the computer is on.
welcome.page1_title: Herdr runs your terminals in the background
welcome.page2_body: Pick a host from your ssh config. Herdr connects, installs herdr-core there if it's missing, and lists that machine in the sidebar with its own spaces.
welcome.page3_body: Herdr comes with a couple of panels. Turn one on and it appears beside your terminals. Drag this window aside to see it. Later, the buttons in the tab bar open and close them.
welcome.page4_body: Every part of this window is a layout or a mod: plain files your agent can change or add to. Give it this line to start:
welcome.panel.changes_about: What your agents changed: every file with its diff, and a commit box.
welcome.panel.files_about: The folder you're in as a tree. Open a file to read it, highlighted.
welcome.panels_ask: Ask your agent for a board of your agents, your pull requests, a cost meter, or the sidebar on the right. Not sure what's possible? Ask it that too.
welcome.then_ask: Then ask for anything: “move the sidebar to the right”, “a panel with my pull requests”.
welcome.title: Welcome to Herdr
settings.alerts.custom: Want your own sounds? Ask your agent to set sounds.done and sounds.blocked in settings.json to an MP3.
settings.alerts.play_sounds.hint: When an agent needs you, and when one finishes while you're not looking. A note shows in the corner either way.
settings.font.layout_own: This layout sets its own; yours shows in the others.
settings.keyboard.hint: Use Option for terminal shortcuts or to type accents and special characters.
settings.language.hint: Chinese or English, or as your system is now.
settings.language.unknown: This Herdr doesn't know {value}; the interface stays in English.
settings.look.appearance.hint: Light or dark, or as your system is now.
settings.look.per_layout: For the layout you're in: each layout keeps its own light and dark theme.
settings.machines.copying: Copying this computer's herdr-core. Its terminals keep running.
settings.machines.intro: Your computers, reached over ssh. Their terminals keep running when you disconnect.
settings.machines.new_name: New name (addresses using the old name stop working)
settings.machines.remove_ask: Remove {name}? Its terminals keep running there.
settings.machines.removed: Removed {name}; its terminals keep running there.
settings.machines.updated_version: Updated {name} to hc {version}; its terminals kept running.
settings.privacy.draft: A draft: it changes until the day ends (UTC), then goes out once.
settings.privacy.exact: Exactly what leaves your computer, word for word.
settings.privacy.off: Off for now: {name} is set where Herdr started.
settings.privacy.quiet: Nothing is collected or sent while it's off.
settings.privacy.share.hint: Once a day: which agents and features you use, how many spaces and tabs, your system and Herdr's version. Never what's in your terminals, never names of files, folders or projects.
settings.privacy.source: This build never sends: it's built from source. You can still see what a release would send.
settings.updates.app_ready: {version} is ready. Restart to switch now; it also switches when you quit.
settings.updates.core_ready: {version} is ready. Your terminals keep running through it.
settings.updates.footer: Herdr looks for both every hour and tells you in the corner. herdr-core runs your terminals, so they keep running through its updates.
settings.updates.no_check: No successful check. Check your connection and try again.
settings.updates.source: A build from source: it updates with git, not here.
settings.updates.source_unchecked: Not checked: a build from source looks for no updates.
